$comment: WP-17: reviewed exemptions from scripts/security/check-migration-security.mjs. Each entry suppresses one rule for one named object and must carry a reason a reviewer can check. Policy, mirroring scripts/security/dependency-audit-allowlist.json: exempt an OBJECT, never a migration file — exempting a file exempts everything anyone adds to it later, including the thing nobody has read yet.

$rules.secdef_search_path: A SECURITY DEFINER function runs with the definer's privileges. Without `SET search_path` the caller chooses which schema an unqualified name resolves in, which turns the function into an escalation primitive.
$rules.secdef_execute: A new SECURITY DEFINER function in `public` is reachable by the publishable key in the browser bundle until EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC AND from `anon` AND from `authenticated`. Both halves cost a production defect and both no-op revokes SUCCEED, so neither reports anything alone. CREATE grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC and every role inherits it, so revoking `anon` alone removes a grant it never had — the RLS-W5 lesson (20260725096000). This project ALSO carries default privileges granting EXECUTE on new functions in `public` directly to `anon` and `authenticated`, so revoking PUBLIC alone leaves those standing: measured on the live catalogue 2026-09-16, `geocode_cache_touch` and `market_sales_refresh` each read `postgres=X | anon=X | authenticated=X | service_role=X` with no PUBLIC entry, both after a migration whose stated purpose was to close them (20261129090000).
$rules.view_security_invoker: A view without `security_invoker = true` reads its base tables with the owner's rights, so RLS on those tables does not apply to anyone who can select the view.
$rules.table_rls: A table created without ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is readable and writable by any role holding a table grant, and PostgREST exposes it.

NOT an exemption from the revoke — 20260913200000 performs it, and the rule is file-scoped so it cannot see that follow-up. Note for whoever reviews this: the object never held the grant. Measured proacl before the revoke was `postgres=X | service_role=X`, because ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES on the `aml` schema grants new functions to service_role only — unlike `public`, whose default grants anon and authenticated. The rule's premise is the Postgres default and does not hold in this schema. It is also a trigger function (RETURNS trigger), so it was never PostgREST-callable.
